name: Hollowborn
homeland: the Burning Sands — the oases, the Glass Reach, the buried cities
language: Hollow Sign (silent trade tongue), plus spoken desert dialects
summary: The people of the dunes and the buried glass. Hollowborn live over a world of entombed cities — the desert swallowed the Concord's southern works whole — and they have made silence, not speech, their mother tongue. They dig, they remember, and they trade in things other people fear to name.
appearance: Lean and sun-hardened, skin dark and lined like cracked earth, eyes pale as the salt-flats.
Cloth wrapped against sand and sun; the hollowborn rarely show their hands, which are scored with the scars of rope, glass, and digging.
Speech is a luxury; many hollowborn are fluent in Hollow Sign before their first spoken word.
temperament: hard, courteous, secretive, generous to fellow travelers

society.government: Oasis-councils of Well-Sisters; caravans govern themselves on the road by the code of the Hollow Sign
society.settlements: Spring-oases ringed by reeds, tent-cities, and the half-excavated mouths of buried Concord cities
society.family: Blood is light; the caravan and the well are family. Names are taken from the oasis or the road where one was born

religion: A defensive pantheon: Ishmet the Burning Crown (appeased), Shardstorm (their war-god), the Hollow Mouth (death, omnipresent), Dhar the Shifting Dune (the luck of the road), Akhmat (mercy, the wells). The Pale Thief — Luneth — is a demon of the night cold, not a god. In secret, the Rememberers keep the Under-Sands: Ithyn under another name.

relations.note: The salt roads pay well and the hollowborn's books worry the Crownlands; trade continues and trust does not.
The deep-folk's pity is returned with quiet amusement; the hollowborn dig deeper than the deep-folk ever will.
Silence speaks to silence. A greenfolk and a hollowborn can converse for an hour without a word and call it a fine meeting.

notes: The Rememberers are the only institution on Aurelith that openly keeps Ithyn's cult — in silence, beneath the sand, where the Edict of Silence cannot reach.
Hollowborn are the greatest excavators of the lost Concord; every buried city is both their heritage and their trade.
They are the one species for whom the Sundering was not a disaster but a legacy — the glass that rings the dunes is beautiful, and they mine it.
